notes: Elicited by launching muse with --base-url pointed at a local port with nothing listening (settings.base_url; requires record to wire this into driver-interactive.sh's launch_repl, currently a stub -- see metadata.json driver_capability: gap:base_url_override), so the first model call fails deterministically and with zero API spend, mirroring copilot's dead-port precedent for this same scenario. Muse's run stream closes every model-call failure with its own terminal:"failed" event (format-spec SS3; two structurally different real captured examples exist on this machine -- an idle-timeout network stall and a config-validation error -- both funnel through the identical shape), which parser.go's parseRunTerminal converts to EventType=turn_done + SessionError. Because muse declares no hooks, HookTurnDone is always false, so state_classifier.go's session_error rule (SessionError!=nil && !HookTurnDone) fires directly and unconditionally, painting the session `error` -- above classifyAgentDone in the authority ladder, and classifyAgentDone independently reaches the identical StateError as a second, converging path. SessionError is sticky: it clears only when the user starts a NEW turn (clearSessionErrorOnRecovery), never on the failing turn's own epilogue -- so unlike every other onboarded agent's 2.14 cell (all of which settle back to ready), muse's real, evidence-based final state is `error`, matching the ready->working->error, Final state: error shape that scenarios 2.23 (provider-overloaded-terminal) and 2.24 (auth-credentials-rejected) define for the architecturally identical underlying event. I judged this the correct, honest daemon_capability=full representation rather than forcing the scenario's literal (but for muse, incorrect) `ready` wording -- see metadata.json body for the full reasoning and the caveats this rests on (elicitation mechanism unconfirmed on a live recording; auth-precondition risk; session-birth shape unconfirmed). Session-birth shape (single birth vs. a transient proc-<PID> pre-session from the daemon's unconditional per-adapter process scanner, wiring.go) is NOT live-confirmed -- session_birth is left UNPINNED to any session (pi-pattern, matching muse/2-13_turn-end-terminal-text's identical open question), and turn_start is anchored to recording start and also unpinned so the matcher picks whichever session first goes working (a pre-session never processes a turn); every phase after turn_start pins via same_session_as so the arc cannot land on a stray pre-session. cost/tokens are asserted false: neither captured failed-turn sample contains a model_completed event before the failure lands.

text: A session (real, or a transient proc-<PID> pre-session) appears in ready within 5s of muse's TUI finishing launch

Every call to the dead --base-url fails; muse's run closes with terminal:"failed", SessionError is set, and the session_error classifier rule paints the session error. State does not stick in working, never touches waiting, and (unlike a normal turn_done) does NOT settle back to ready on its own -- the failure is sticky until the user's next turn, which this recipe never sends.
